lines.text: Here's a real project, pinning one outside piece at one exact version, the ordinary way any project pins anything.
Nobody on this project went looking for trouble in that specific piece. Does a real, published list of known problems catch it anyway, with no help at all?
Yes, genuinely.
The list doesn't need to be told what to look for. It already knows.
Run it for real: that exact pinned piece comes back flagged, by its own real name, straight from a real, public record nobody on this project had to write themselves.
Now bump to the very next real release of that exact same piece, the one the record itself says was actually fixed.
Does the identical check still flag it, just for having once had a problem at all?
No, it doesn't.
What's checked is the exact version sitting there right now, not some lingering reputation.
Run it for real: the newer release comes back completely clean, from the identical real check that flagged the older one.
Put both real results side by side: the exact same outside piece, one version apart.
Did the real list actually tell those two versions apart, or did it just flag the piece as a whole?
It told them apart.
Only the one real version with a genuine, known problem gets flagged. The other one doesn't.
Run it for real: one exact version comes back flagged, the very next one comes back clean, from the identical real check run against both.
One real, public page describes exactly this, in its own plain words.
A real record of known problems, kept for the whole real community that builds in this language, and a real tool that checks one project's own exact, pinned versions against it directly.
So here's what this topic's own two real checks were really standing in for: swap one number in a version string, and the honest answer you get back can flip completely.
Nothing about how recently it shipped, or how long it's been sitting there without complaint, tells you which one is actually safe.
Only a real, kept-up-to-date record, actually checked against, on purpose, every time, can tell you that.
